Interface ChaosSession

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
public interface ChaosSession extends AutoCloseable
A named session scope that restricts chaos effects to the threads bound to it.

Sessions enable per-test isolation when multiple tests share a single JVM: each test opens its own session, activates scenarios scoped to that session, and only threads bound to that session observe chaos. Threads without a binding are unaffected.

The thread that opens a session (ChaosControlPlane.openSession(String)) is bound to it from then until close(); other threads join it with bind(), and work handed off from a bound thread carries it (executor tasks, fork-join tasks, started threads).

Basic usage: 

try (ChaosSession session = controlPlane.openSession("my-test")) {
    session.activate(scenario);
    // the opening thread is bound: operations on it are intercepted by the session scenario
    myService.call();
}
// session is closed: its scenarios are stopped and the opening thread is unbound

A thread the session did not hand work to (a server's request thread, a callback thread) joins it for a block: 

try (ChaosSession.ScopeBinding binding = session.bind()) {
    myService.call(); // intercepted by the session scenario
}
// this thread is unbound again

Cross-thread propagation: use wrap(Runnable) or wrap(Callable) to propagate the session context into executor threads: 

executor.submit(session.wrap(() -> {
    // session context is active on this executor thread during the task
    myService.call();
}));

Sessions are created via ChaosControlPlane.openSession(String).

  • Field Details

    • HEADER

      static final String HEADER
      The HTTP header that carries a session id between services. Requests the JDK HttpClient or HttpURLConnection sends from a thread bound to a session carry it automatically; a server binds the request to the session with ChaosControlPlane.bindSession(String) (the Spring Boot starters register a filter for that).

    • activate

      ChaosActivationHandle activate(ChaosScenario scenario)
      Activates a SESSION-scoped scenario within this session. Only threads bound to this session are affected: the thread that opened it, until close(), and threads bound with bind().
      Parameters:
      scenario - must have ChaosScenario.ScenarioScope.SESSION scope; JVM-scoped scenarios cannot be activated on a session
      Returns:
      a handle for per-scenario lifecycle control
      Throws:
      ChaosActivationException - if the scenario scope is not SESSION
      ChaosValidationException - if the scenario fails validation
      ChaosUnsupportedFeatureException - if the scenario requires more than the runtime provides
      ChaosActivationConflictException - if a scenario with the same ID is still registered or active in this session
      ChaosInstrumentationException - if the instrumentation the scenario needs cannot be woven
      IllegalStateException - if the session or its control plane is closed

    • activate

      ChaosActivationHandle activate(ChaosPlan plan)
      Activates all scenarios in the given ChaosPlan within this session. All scenarios in the plan must be SESSION-scoped.
      Parameters:
      plan - all scenarios must be SESSION-scoped
      Returns:
      a composite handle controlling all scenarios in the plan
      Throws:
      ChaosActivationException - if a scenario in the plan is not SESSION-scoped
      ChaosValidationException - if a scenario fails validation
      ChaosUnsupportedFeatureException - if a scenario requires more than the runtime provides
      ChaosActivationConflictException - if a scenario's ID is still registered or active in this session
      ChaosInstrumentationException - if the instrumentation the plan needs cannot be woven
      IllegalStateException - if the session or its control plane is closed

    • bind

      ChaosSession.ScopeBinding bind()
      Binds the calling thread to this session, making it eligible for session-scoped chaos. The thread that opened the session is bound already; use this on other threads.

      The binding is stored in a thread-local and remains active until ChaosSession.ScopeBinding.close() is called. Nested bind() calls on the same thread stack: the innermost binding applies until it is closed, then the one beneath it applies again.

      Always use in try-with-resources to guarantee the thread is unbound: 

      try (ChaosSession.ScopeBinding binding = session.bind()) {
    // this thread is in scope
}
      Returns:
      a ChaosSession.ScopeBinding that removes the binding when closed

    • wrap

      Runnable wrap(Runnable runnable)
      Wraps a Runnable so that it executes with this session's scope active on whatever thread runs it.

      Use this when submitting work to an executor pool: the wrapped task carries the session context into the pool thread, enabling session-scoped chaos on executor operations.

      Parameters:
      runnable - the task to wrap; must not be null
      Returns:
      a new Runnable that activates the session context before delegating to the original
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if runnable is null

    • wrap

      <T> Callable<T> wrap(Callable<T> callable)
      Wraps a Callable so that it executes with this session's scope active on whatever thread runs it.
      Type Parameters:
      T - the return type of the callable
      Parameters:
      callable - the task to wrap; must not be null
      Returns:
      a new Callable that activates the session context before delegating to the original
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if callable is null

    • close

      void close()
      Stops all session-scoped scenarios and releases the session, ending the binding of the thread that opened it. After this call, threads previously bound to this session will no longer observe session-scoped chaos.
      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
